summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: @hubsync/web-sdk-react@6.3.30 ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun (v1.3.13) into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` file consisting of a large numeric/string array plus a rotation decoder (`WV8StW` repeatedly performing `push(shift())` on the array) — a standard string-array obfuscator. The payload is executed only through the freshly downloaded Bun binary, so Node-based analysis of the module never observes what the decoded code does. The package is published under the `@hubsync` scope but its `package.json` description is 'Verdocs Web SDK for React' and its dist bundle references `https://api.verdocs.com`, indicating the dropper is grafted onto a repackaged copy of an unrelated vendor's SDK. Fetching an alternate language runtime at install time solely to run an opaque obfuscated bundled blob is the alternate-runtime-dropper install-time RCE pattern; a React SDK has no legitimate need for Bun.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
